r2_status.G-6: OPEN: §8 correctly refuses an unversioned case, but §12 still requires `run-cohort.sh --case taskrun --config cheap` to succeed, leaving acceptance and implementation contradictory.

findings.claim: The acceptance criteria reintroduce the unsafe newest-version behavior that §8 explicitly prohibits, so an implementer cannot know whether an unpinned cohort command must succeed or be refused.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:206-210 requires `--case` to contain `@version` everywhere and says unpinned input is refused; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:272-274 requires `run-cohort.sh --case taskrun --config cheap` to provision. Current cohort state becomes durable only after identity selection at benchmark/run-cohort.sh:193-230.
findings.fix: Change §12 to use `--case taskrun@0.1`; keep unpinned cases refused for cohorts, proposals, provisioning, extraction, and grading unless a separately named ad-hoc command is deliberately introduced.

findings.claim: The compatibility table refuses four shipped legacy aliases. Their boolean gate has cycles=8 and ledgerNoGainBudget=5, but none declares acceptBinaryGateFuse; §6 therefore classifies them as incompatible despite promising validation of every alias pair.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:157 requires `ledgerNoGainBudget >= cycles` or `acceptBinaryGateFuse`; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:25-28 identifies bm-2, bm-2d, bm-2dc and bm-2d-og as boolean-gate configurations with cycles=8/no-gain=5; their manifests omit `fences.acceptBinaryGateFuse`, for example benchmark/specs/bm-2/manifest.json:135-143. The design requires every alias pair to pass compatibility at metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:147 and acceptance at :270-272.
findings.fix: Preserve legacy admission explicitly: either assign a sourced legacy acknowledgement to those four configurations, exempt migrated aliases from this new launch policy, or make the fuse check apply only to newly authored configurations. Add positive fixtures for all six aliases as well as negative fixtures for new invalid configurations.

findings.claim: Recording caseTree does not prevent two different case trees from being compared as the same case version because §3 omits caseTree from the comparability tuple and §7 does not require cohort-to-scorecard equality for it.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:50-54 says caseTree prevents later edits being mistaken for old content, but :81-87 defines the complete comparability tuple without caseTree. Current compare logic explicitly constructs and compares its tuple at benchmark/compare.py:164-175 and separately joins selected scorecard identity fields to the cohort record at benchmark/compare.py:200-223; an implementer following the stated replacement would likewise omit the new field.
findings.fix: Put caseTree, including its algorithm/kind and dirty marker, in cohort records and scorecards; require exact cohort-to-scorecard equality and include it in verdict comparability. Extractor validation must recompute or otherwise authenticate it against the case content used for extraction.

findings.claim: Proposal and eligibility evaluation is tied to the current configuration file rather than the configuration version that produced the run. Because each configuration has one mutable pathname with history only in git, bumping it makes valid archived proposals and cohorts fail the mandated version-equality check on another machine at a newer checkout.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:62-64 stores one `configurations/<id>.json` and says prior versions live in git; :185-192 says compare loads that pathname and requires its current version to equal the proposal's named version. Current ancestry validation already has the candidate SHA at benchmark/compare.py:259-300, while current eligibility reads the installed manifest rather than historical content at benchmark/compare.py:529-544.
findings.fix: Define historical lookup: load case and configuration JSON from the recorded measuringMetasystemSha or caseTree/config tree identity, then validate proposal membership and eligibility against those bytes. Document and fixture comparison after the working checkout has advanced to a newer configuration version.

findings.claim: The dirty caseTree fallback is not implementable reproducibly: the design does not define when a checkout is considered dirty, which files are included, canonical record framing, symlink handling, or the representation distinguishing a Git tree SHA from a SHA-256 directory digest. Unrelated working-tree dirt can also switch the identity algorithm for unchanged case content.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:50-54 specifies `git rev-parse` in a clean checkout and otherwise only 'sha256 over the directory's sorted paths, exec bits and bytes, marked dirty.' Git tree identity already accounts for paths, executable modes and bytes, while current cohort identity pins a repository SHA at benchmark/run-cohort.sh:177-178.
findings.fix: Use the Git tree SHA whenever the selected case subtree matches HEAD, regardless of unrelated dirt. For modified or untracked case content, preferably refuse durable cohort provisioning; if dirty ad-hoc runs are required, define a versioned canonical tree encoding, symlink policy, digest algorithm, and structured `{kind,value,dirty}` representation.

summary: R3 closes the round-2 projection, resume, documentation-schema, title, mission-id, and self-referential-digest findings, and its bounded static instrument tag is operationally acceptable because the sealed contract authenticates the actual instrument bytes. It still cannot be implemented safely as written: acceptance contradicts the pinned-case rule, the compatibility law refuses four legacy aliases, caseTree is recorded but excluded from comparison joins, historical configuration versions cannot be reconstructed after a bump, and the dirty-tree identity algorithm is underspecified. The migration does not need an embedded immutability digest, but it does need a single reproducible historical identity path and positive compatibility proof for every alias.
